mainTopic: כרת for missing פסח ראשון and פסח שני, and the definition of דרך רחוקה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a מחלוקת about which פסח carries כרת. רבי learns כרת for skipping פסח שני from a גזרה שוה on the word ״חטאו״, because he holds that the מגדף is the same as one who curses ה׳. רבי נתן reads ״כי״ as "because," so the כרת is for the first פסח, and he runs the same גזרה שוה in the other direction to teach כרת for cursing ה׳. רבי חנניא בן עקביא reads the verse so that כרת depends on also missing פסח שני. The גמרא then charts all four combinations of skipping on purpose or by accident on each פסח. A new משנה asks what counts as a דרך רחוקה: רבי עקיבא says from מודיעין and beyond, while רבי אליעזר says anywhere outside the עזרה, and רבי יוסי supports him from the dot over the ה. In the גמרא, עולא explains that מודיעין is 15 מיל away, the distance a person walks from sunrise to midday, so a traveler there cannot arrive by the time of שחיטה. רב יהודה instead measures by the time of eating. רבה challenges both views from the case of a טמא שרץ. עולא answers that the far-journey rule applies only to a טהור person, and his defense of רב יהודה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי's premise: the blasphemer and the one who curses ה׳ are the same
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that מגדף (where the Torah says כרת) is the same sin as מברך את השם (where the Torah says ״ונשא חטאו״).
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבי) holds that the מגדף is the same as one who curses ("blesses") ה׳'s name. And about one who curses ה׳'s name, it is written "and he shall bear his sin."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining how רבי knows that the words ״חטאו ישא״ mean כרת. It starts with his premise: two verses that look different are actually describing one sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about the מגדף (במדבר ט״ו:ל׳) explicitly says ״ונכרתה״. The verse about מברך את השם (ויקרא כ״ד:ט״ו) says ״ונשא חטאו״. If these are the same sin, then ״נשא חטאו״ must be a way of describing כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (his reasoning is)
Blasphemer; the verse about him states כרת
Literally "blesses the Name"; a polite way of saying one who curses ה׳
"And he shall bear his sin"

steps.confusionAlert: ״מברך השם״ does NOT mean someone who blesses ה׳. It is a respectful way of saying the opposite (cursing), so that the text avoids writing the ugly words.

phrases.english: He holds: the blasphemer is the same as
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי, whose view is being explained

phrases.english: one who "blesses" (curses) the Name,
and it is written about one who curses the Name
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא כ״ד:ט״ו.

phrases.english: "and he shall bear his sin."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of רבי's view, which began on the previous amud
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״נשא חטאו״ is tied to כרת because מגדף and מברך את השם are one sin

steps.title: רבי's verbal link: "his sin" by פסח means כרת
steps.stepSummary: Using a גזרה שוה, רבי learns that ״חטאו״ in the פסח verse means כרת, just like ״חטאו״ by the one who curses ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns this word "his sin" here (by פסח) from "his sin" there (by the one who curses ה׳). Just as there it means כרת, so too here it also means כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי finishes his proof. He links the word ״חטאו״ in the פסח verse to the same word by מברך את השם, so the פסח case also gets כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed that ״חטאו״ by מברך את השם means כרת. Now the shared word ״חטאו״ carries that meaning over to פסח. Since רבי reads ״חטאו ישא״ as speaking about פסח שני, he concludes that skipping פסח שני carries כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: And he learns (derives), here through a גזרה שוה
Of here / of there
Just as there... so too here (the formula of a גזרה שוה)
Spiritual cutting off; a heavenly punishment

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: מגדף = מברך את השם, so ״חטאו״ means כרת there. The גזרה שוה then gives כרת to ״חטאו ישא״ by פסח.

phrases.english: And he learns this "his sin" of here (Pesach)
from "his sin" of there (one who curses ה׳):
just as there it is כרת,
so too here it is also כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof that step 1 began
steps.raayaObject: That ״חטאו ישא״ by פסח means כרת
steps.raayaSupportSource: גזרה שוה with ״ונשא חטאו״ by מברך את השם (ויקרא כ״ד:ט״ו)

steps.title: רבי נתן reads ״כי״ as "because": the כרת is for the first פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן reads the verse so that the כרת applies only to missing the first פסח, with ״כי״ meaning "because."
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי נתן holds: "and he refrains from doing the פסח, he shall be cut off." This word "כי" means "because." This is what the Torah is saying: because "he did not bring ה׳'s offering in its time," meaning on the first פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the other side of the מחלוקת. It shows how רבי נתן reads the same verse differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נתן, the clause with ״כי״ gives the reason for the כרת already stated earlier in the verse. It does not start a new case about פסח שני. So the כרת is about missing the first פסח, and the verse says nothing here about כרת for פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he refrains from doing the פסח" (במדבר ט׳:י״ג)
A word that can mean "if" or "because"
A term meaning "because"
In its set time
On the first (פסח)

steps.confusionAlert: The whole argument depends on the word ״כי״. For רבי it opens a new case ("if" he did not bring it on פסח שני). For רבי נתן it explains the earlier כרת ("because" he did not bring it on the first פסח).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Natan holds:
"and he refrains from doing the Pesach, that soul shall be cut off,"
for this "ki" is an expression of "because,"
and this is what the Merciful One (the Torah) says:
because "he did not bring the offering of ה׳ in its appointed time"
on the first (Pesach).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing reading after רבי's derivation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נתן, the כרת in the verse is for missing the first פסח, since ״כי״ means "because"

steps.title: What does רבי נתן do with ״חטאו ישא״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what purpose the words ״חטאו ישא״ serve for רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This phrase "he shall bear his sin" — what does he (רבי נתן) do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי נתן uses ״חטאו ישא״, since he does not use these words for פסח שני. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, these words taught כרת for פסח שני. For רבי נתן, the כרת is already stated outright in the verse. So these words seem extra, and every word in the Torah must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (what does he learn from this phrase?)
"He shall bear his sin"

phrases.english: This "he shall bear his sin"
what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רבי נתן's reading accounts for the phrase that רבי used
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי נתן learns from ״חטאו ישא״

steps.title: רבי נתן: the מגדף is a different sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן holds that מגדף is not the same as מברך את השם, so the Torah never states the punishment for cursing ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבי נתן) holds that the מגדף is not the same as one who curses ה׳'s name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by showing that רבי נתן disagrees with רבי's premise from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נתן, the verse saying כרת (מגדף) is about a different sin. So the ״ונשא חטאו״ by מברך את השם has no clear meaning on its own and needs a source. This prepares the reversed גזרה שוה in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not the same as

phrases.english: He holds: the blasphemer is not the same as
one who "blesses" (curses) the Name,

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: מְגַדֵּף לָאו הַיְינוּ מְבָרֵךְ אֶת הַשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering step 4 by rejecting רבי's premise from step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מגדף and מברך את השם are separate sins, so the punishment for מברך את השם must be learned from somewhere else

steps.title: רבי נתן reverses the verbal link: from פסח to one who curses ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן uses ״חטאו ישא״ by פסח, which sits right next to an explicit כרת, to teach that ״חטאו״ by מברך את השם means כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns "his sin" there (by one who curses ה׳) from "his sin" here (by פסח). Just as here it is כרת, so too there it is כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its answer. רבי נתן uses the same גזרה שוה as רבי, but in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By פסח, the verse states ״ונכרתה״ outright, so ״חטאו ישא״ there clearly means כרת. That meaning then passes to ״ונשא חטאו״ by מברך את השם. So the phrase is not extra: it is the source for כרת for cursing ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as here... so too there

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים use the same גזרה שוה on ״חטאו״, but in opposite directions. רבי: from מברך את השם to פסח, which gives כרת for פסח שני. רבי נתן: from פסח to מברך את השם, which gives כרת for cursing ה׳.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the same שני כתובים can be linked in either direction. The direction depends on which verse already has a clear punishment. That in turn depends on each תנא's reading of מגדף and of ״כי״.

phrases.english: And he learns this "his sin" of there (one who curses ה׳)
from this "his sin" of here (Pesach).
Just as here it is כרת —
so too there it is כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to step 4 by reversing רבי's גזרה שוה from step 2
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי נתן, ״חטאו ישא״ by פסח is not extra. It is the source for כרת for one who curses ה׳.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי נתן uses ״חטאו ישא״ by פסח, which sits beside an explicit ״ונכרתה״, as the source for כרת for one who curses ה׳ (reversing רבי's גזרה שוה).

steps.title: A third reading: the כרת depends on the second פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בן עקביא reads the verse so that כרת applies only if the person also failed to bring the קרבן on פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנניא בן עקביא holds: 'He refrained from doing the פסח and will be cut off,' if 'he did not bring ה׳'s offering in its time.' This means on the second פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a third way to read the verse, from רבי חנניא בן עקביא. For him, the כרת only comes if the person also missed פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן said the כרת is about missing the first פסח, reading ״כי״ as 'because.' רבי חנניא בן עקביא reads ״כי״ as 'if' (אי), and he says 'its time' refers to the second פסח. So skipping the first פסח is not enough for כרת until the person also fails to make it up on פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: And he refrained; he held back from doing it
And (that soul) will be cut off. This is the punishment of כרת.
If. Here it explains how to read the word ״כי״ in the verse.
In its appointed time
The second chance to bring the פסח, one month later

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the three opinions. רבי נתן links the כרת to the FIRST פסח. רבי חנניא בן עקביא links it to the SECOND פסח.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya holds:
'And he refrained from doing the Pesach, and that soul will be cut off,'

phrases.aramaic: אִי ״קׇרְבַּן ה׳ לֹא הִקְרִיב בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ״ — בַּשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.english: if 'he did not bring ה׳'s offering in its appointed time,' meaning on the second (Pesach).
phrases.notes: ״כי״ is read as 'if,' and 'its appointed time' is taken to mean פסח שני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רבי נתן's reading, the גמרא presents a third opinion's reading of the same verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי חנניא בן עקביא, כרת for the פסח depends on failing to bring it on פסח שני.

steps.title: What does he do with ״חטאו ישא״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי חנניא בן עקביא learns from the words ״חטאו ישא״, since he does not use them for the פסח punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this phrase ״חטאו ישא״, what does he do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question it asked about רבי נתן: what is the purpose of ״חטאו ישא״ for this opinion? It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנניא בן עקביא already gets the כרת from ״ונכרתה״, which is written explicitly. So the extra words ״חטאו ישא״ seem to have no job in his reading, and the גמרא wants to know what they teach.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall bear his sin
What does he do with it? That is, what does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And this phrase 'he shall bear his sin'
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי חֶטְאוֹ יִשָּׂא מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks about the leftover words in the verse that was just read in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי חנניא בן עקביא learns from ״חטאו ישא״.

steps.title: Same as רבי נתן: it teaches the punishment for cursing ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The answer is 'as we said': like רבי נתן, he uses ״חטאו ישא״ to teach that the one who curses ה׳ gets כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers briefly by pointing back to what it already explained. רבי חנניא בן עקביא uses ״חטאו ישא״ exactly the way רבי נתן did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 5-6, רבי נתן held that the Torah never states the punishment for מברך את השם. He learned it from ״חטאו ישא״ by פסח, which sits right next to an explicit כרת. The one-word answer ״כדאמרן״ tells us that רבי חנניא בן עקביא holds the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: As we said; it refers back to an earlier explanation
One who curses ה׳ (a polite way of saying it)

phrases.english: As we said (earlier).
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי נתן's use of ״חטאו ישא״ for the one who curses ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He uses ״חטאו ישא״ like רבי נתן does, to teach that the one who curses ה׳ gets כרת.

steps.title: The cases where all opinions agree
steps.stepSummary: Therefore: skipping both times on purpose means everyone says חייב. Missing both times by accident means everyone says פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore: if he acted on purpose in this one and in that one, all agree he is liable. If he acted by accident in this one and in that one, all agree he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts summing up the practical results of the three readings. It begins with the two cases where everyone agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person skipped both the first and second פסח on purpose, every reading leads to כרת. If he missed both by accident, no reading gives כרת, since כרת only comes for doing it on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore; this introduces the practical results
He acted on purpose
He acted by accident or by mistake
Everyone agrees
Liable (gets כרת) / exempt

phrases.english: Therefore: if he acted intentionally in this one and in that one (both Pesachs),
all agree he is liable;
if he acted unintentionally in this one and in that one,
all agree he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that all three readings have been explained, it draws practical results from them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Skipping both on purpose means כרת for everyone. Missing both by accident means no כרת for anyone.

steps.title: The disputed case: on purpose the first time, by accident the second
steps.stepSummary: If a person skipped the first פסח on purpose but missed the second by accident, רבי and רבי נתן say he is liable. רבי חנניא בן עקביא says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he acted on purpose on the first and by accident on the second, according to רבי and רבי נתן he is liable. According to רבי חנניא בן עקביא, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the summary with the case where the opinions split. It shows exactly how the different readings of the verse lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי and רבי נתן, skipping the first פסח on purpose already earns כרת, so missing the second by accident does not save him. For רבי חנניא בן עקביא, the כרת depends on the second פסח. Since the second was missed by accident, he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: On the first (פסח)
They hold him liable

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument comes down to which פסח the כרת is linked to. רבי and רבי נתן look at the first פסח. רבי חנניא בן עקביא looks at the second פסח. That is why only the case of 'on purpose first, by accident second' is disputed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a small reading choice in a verse, such as what ״כי״ means and what 'its time' refers to, leads directly to a real practical difference in who gets כרת.

phrases.english: If he acted intentionally on the first and unintentionally on the second,
according to Rabbi and Rabbi Natan, they hold him liable;
according to Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It continues the summary from step 10, moving from the cases everyone agrees on to the case they dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: On purpose the first time and by accident the second time: liable according to רבי and רבי נתן, exempt according to רבי חנניא בן עקביא.

steps.title: Accidental first, intentional second: only רבי says liable
steps.stepSummary: The last case in the chart: a person missed פסח ראשון by accident and skipped פסח שני on purpose. רבי says חייב. רבי נתן and רבי חנניא בן עקביא say פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made an innocent mistake on the first פסח and acted on purpose on the second, according to רבי he is liable. According to רבי נתן and רבי חנניא בן עקביא he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its chart of all four combinations by giving the last one: accident on the first פסח, on purpose on the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי treats פסח שני as its own holiday with its own כרת, so skipping it on purpose is enough to be liable. רבי נתן gives כרת only for skipping the first פסח on purpose, and here the first was an accident. רבי חנניא בן עקביא needs both to be on purpose, so he also says פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Did it by accident or mistake
Did it on purpose
Liable (here, to כרת)
Exempt

steps.whatToRemember: The full chart: on purpose both times, everyone says חייב. Accident both times, everyone says פטור. On purpose first and accident second: רבי and רבי נתן say חייב, רבי חנניא says פטור. Accident first and on purpose second: only רבי says חייב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this case with the one in Step 11. There the first פסח was skipped on purpose, so רבי נתן said חייב. Here the first was an accident, so רבי נתן now says פטור.

phrases.english: If he erred by accident on the first and acted on purpose on the second,
according to Rabbi, he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי נָתָן וּלְרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא — פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Natan and Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of cases begun in Steps 10 and 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only רבי, who sees פסח שני as its own independent holiday, gives כרת for skipping פסח שני on purpose after missing the first by accident.

steps.title: New משנה: רבי עקיבא defines a far journey as from מודיעין and beyond
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה asks what counts as דרך רחוקה. רבי עקיבא answers: from מודיעין and beyond, and the same distance in every direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: What is a 'far journey'? From מודיעין and outward, and the same distance in every direction. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks how far from ירושלים a person must be to count as 'on a far journey', which exempts him from the first פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה exempts someone on a דרך רחוקה from bringing the פסח on time. רבי עקיבא sets a fixed distance: the distance of the town of מודיעין from ירושלים, measured in any direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A far-away journey (the תורה's exemption from the first פסח)
מודיעין, a town some distance from ירושלים
In every direction

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
What is a 'far journey'?
From Modi'im and outward,
and the same distance in every direction —
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, a דרך רחוקה is the distance of מודיעין from ירושלים or more, in any direction.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: anywhere outside the עזרה counts as far
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees with רבי עקיבא. Anyone outside the threshold of the עזרה at the time of שחיטה counts as being on a דרך רחוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: from the threshold of the עזרה and outward.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה. רבי אליעזר makes the 'far' zone much bigger: it starts right at the doorway of the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, 'far' does not mean a fixed number of miles. If the person is not inside the עזרה when the קרבן is slaughtered, he is exempt from the first פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: The threshold (doorway) of the Temple courtyard
And outward / beyond

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
From the threshold of the Temple courtyard and outward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי עקיבא's definition in Step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, anyone outside the עזרה at the time of שחיטה counts as being on a דרך רחוקה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי supports רבי אליעזר from the dot over the ה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says this is why the ה in the word רחֹקה has a dot over it. The dot tells us 'far' is not meant literally; it starts at the threshold of the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: That is why there is a dot over the ה. It comes to say: not because he is truly far away, but from the threshold of the עזרה and outward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי backs up רבי אליעזר's view with a proof from how the word is written in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the word רחֹקה has a dot written over the ה. רבי יוסי reads the dot as a signal not to take 'far' at face value. The person does not need to be truly far away; being outside the עזרה is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore / that is why
Dotted (marked with a dot over a letter in the ספר תורה)
Truly / definitely

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
That is why there is a dot over the letter heh,
to say: not because he is truly far away,
but rather from the threshold of the courtyard and outward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְפִיכָךְ נָקוּד עַל ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from the פסוק for רבי אליעזר's view
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that 'far' begins at the threshold of the עזרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dot written over the ה in the word רחֹקה in the פסוק

steps.title: עולא: מודיעין is fifteen מיל from ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with עולא's statement that the distance from מודיעין to ירושלים is 15 מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: עולא said: From מודיעין to ירושלים is fifteen מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the משנה by measuring רבי עקיבא's boundary: how far is מודיעין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא turns רבי עקיבא's place name into a number: 15 מיל. The next steps explain why 15 is the right number.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of distance (about 1 km), 2,000 אמות
Fifteen

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Ulla said:
From Modi'im to Jerusalem
is fifteen mil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי עקיבא's boundary from Step 13

steps.title: How far a person walks in a day: the source of the 15
steps.stepSummary: עולא follows רבי יוחנן's rule that a person walks 40 מיל in a day. That breaks down to 5 before sunrise, 5 after sunset, 15 from morning to midday, and 15 from midday to evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like what רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: How far does a person walk in a day? Ten פרסאות. From dawn until sunrise, five מיל. From sunset until the stars come out, five מיל. That leaves thirty: fifteen from morning to midday, and fifteen from midday to evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where עולא's number 15 comes from: a standard rule about how far an average person walks in one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten פרסאות equal 40 מיל. Take away 5 for dawn to sunrise and 5 for sunset to the stars coming out, and 30 are left for the daytime. That is 15 for the morning and 15 for the afternoon. So 15 מיל is exactly what a person walks from sunrise until midday.

keyTerms.meaning: A Persian mile, equal to 4 מיל
Dawn
Sunrise
When the stars come out
Midday

steps.confusionAlert: The 40 מיל are not split evenly across the whole day. The two short twilight periods take 5 מיל each, and only the remaining 30 are split between morning and afternoon.

phrases.english: He holds like this teaching
that Rabba bar bar Chana said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
How far does a person walk in a day?
Ten parasangs (forty mil):
from dawn until sunrise
five mil;
from sunset until the stars come out
five mil.
Thirty are left:
fifteen from morning until midday,
and fifteen from midday until evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis for עולא's 15 מיל in Step 16
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's rule (through רבה בר בר חנה) that a person walks 40 מיל a day, 15 of them from morning to midday

steps.title: עולא's definition: too far to arrive by the time of שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: עולא is consistent with his own view. He defines דרך רחוקה as any place from which a person cannot get into the עזרה by the time of שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא follows his own reasoning, as עולא said: What is a far journey? Any place from which a person cannot enter by the time of the slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why עולא tied 15 מיל to the walking day: it matches his own definition of 'far'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח is slaughtered starting after midday. Someone 15 מיל away in the morning needs the whole morning just to walk there, so he cannot arrive in time for the start of שחיטה. That is why מודיעין, at 15 מיל, marks the line of דרך רחוקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own (known) reasoning
The time the קרבן is slaughtered
To enter (the עזרה)

steps.whatToRemember: For עולא, 'far' is about timing, not plain distance: a person is far if he cannot reach the עזרה by the time of שחיטה. Since 15 מיל takes from sunrise to midday to walk, מודיעין is the boundary.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns רבי עקיבא's place name into a clear rule: being 'far' means being unable to arrive in time.

phrases.english: Ulla follows his own reasoning,
for Ulla said:
What is a far journey?
Any place from which one cannot enter
by the time of the slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties עולא's 15 מיל to his own definition of דרך רחוקה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A דרך רחוקה is any distance from which a person cannot reach the עזרה by the time of שחיטה.

steps.title: What is the source for 5 מיל between dawn and sunrise?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes one piece of the walking schedule and asks how we know it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: from dawn until sunrise a person walks five מיל. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to one detail of רבי יוחנן's 40-מיל schedule and asks for its source. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 we were told that a person walks 5 מיל before sunrise. Now the גמרא wants to know where that number comes from. It is not challenging the number. It only wants a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Dawn, when the first light appears
Sunrise, when the sun itself appears
'How do we know?' — a request for a source

phrases.english: The Master said:
From dawn until sunrise
is five mil (of walking).
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מֵעֲלוֹת הַשַּׁחַר עַד הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה חֲמֵשֶׁת מִילִין, מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to one part of the schedule in step 17 and asks for its source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the time between dawn and sunrise equals 5 מיל of walking

steps.title: The verses about לוט leaving סדום
steps.stepSummary: The verses show that לוט left סדום at dawn and reached צוער at sunrise.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And when the dawn rose, the angels urged [לוט]…', and it is written: 'The sun had risen upon the earth when לוט came to צוער.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two verses. They show that לוט's walk from סדום to צוער took exactly the time from dawn to sunrise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first verse sets the start of the trip at dawn, when the angels hurried לוט out. The second verse sets the end at sunrise, when he arrived in צוער. So the distance from סדום to צוער is exactly one dawn-to-sunrise walk. We still need to know how far that is, and the next step tells us.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They urged / hurried' — the angels rushing לוט out
The town that לוט fled to
'Etc.' — the verse continues

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And when the dawn rose,
the angels urged [Lot] on, etc.'
And it is written: 'The sun had risen upon the earth
when Lot came to Zoar.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The walk from סדום to צוער took exactly the time from dawn to sunrise

steps.title: רבי חנינא measured the distance at 5 מיל
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says he saw the place himself, and it is 5 מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנינא said: I myself saw that place, and it is five מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא supplies the missing piece. The distance from סדום to צוער is 5 מיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses showed that the trip took from dawn to sunrise. Now we learn that the trip covers 5 מיל. Put the two facts together and a person walks 5 מיל between dawn and sunrise.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I myself saw it' — an eyewitness report
Place
A unit of distance, about 2,000 אמות

steps.whatToRemember: Dawn to sunrise equals 5 מיל of walking. We know this because לוט walked from סדום to צוער in that time, and that route is 5 מיל.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina said:
I myself saw that place,
and it is five mil.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי הָהוּא אַתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof by giving the actual distance
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא's eyewitness measurement of the distance from סדום to צוער

steps.title: עולא's definition of a far journey, restated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back עולא's statement so it can discuss it in detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the matter itself: עולא said: What is a דרך רחוקה? Anyone who cannot enter by the time of slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא returns to עולא's main statement and quotes it again. It does this to set up a disagreement and a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same ruling we saw in step 18. Here it is repeated on purpose, so that רב יהודה's opposing view can be placed next to it. According to עולא, the key moment is the time of slaughtering.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself' — the גמרא returns to discuss a statement it quoted earlier
A 'far journey', which exempts a person from the first פסח
The time when the פסח is slaughtered

phrases.english: To the matter itself: Ulla said:
What is a 'distant journey'?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לִיכָּנֵס בִּשְׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה.
phrases.english: Anyone who cannot enter (the עזרה) at the time of slaughtering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side topic of walking times to עולא's main ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דרך רחוקה means being unable to reach the עזרה by the time of slaughtering

steps.title: רב יהודה: the measure is the time of eating
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה defines a far journey by whether the person can arrive in time to eat the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: Anyone who cannot enter by the time of eating.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a different definition. He looks at whether the person can get to ירושלים by the night of eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא looks at the afternoon slaughtering. רב יהודה looks at the night, when the פסח is eaten. According to רב יהודה, if you can arrive in time to eat, you are not on a דרך רחוקה, even if you miss the slaughtering.

keyTerms.meaning: The time when the פסח is eaten, on the night after it is slaughtered

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. עולא = slaughtering time (afternoon). רב יהודה = eating time (night).

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לִיכָּנֵס בִּשְׁעַת אֲכִילָה.
phrases.english: Anyone who cannot enter at the time of eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לִיכָּנֵס בִּשְׁעַת אֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing definition to עולא's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דרך רחוקה means being unable to reach ירושלים by the time of eating

steps.title: רבה announces a difficulty for both views
steps.stepSummary: רבה tells עולא that both his view and רב יהודה's view have a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to עולא: There is a difficulty for you, and there is a difficulty for רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבה announces that he has challenges for both opinions, and he lays them out in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has been proven yet. רבה is only signaling a two-part attack. Each part will show that one of these views clashes with what that same אמורא says elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to you'
'It is difficult' — a challenge

phrases.english: Rabba said to Ulla:
For you there is a difficulty, and for Rav Yehuda there is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה לְעוּלָּא: לְדִידָךְ קַשְׁיָא וּלְרַב יְהוּדָה קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces challenges to both definitions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The details come in steps 25–26.

steps.title: Challenge to עולא from a טמא שרץ
steps.stepSummary: A טמא שרץ also cannot enter at slaughtering time, yet עולא allows the פסח to be slaughtered for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: For you it is difficult, since you said: anyone who cannot enter at the time of slaughtering. But a טמא שרץ cannot enter at the time of slaughtering, and yet you said: we slaughter and sprinkle the blood for a טמא שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה shows that עולא seems to contradict himself. Someone who touched a שרץ also cannot enter the עזרה at slaughtering time, yet עולא lets us bring the פסח for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא treats being unable to enter at slaughtering time as the reason a traveler is on a דרך רחוקה and exempt. A טמא שרץ is in the same position, since his impurity keeps him out until nightfall. Even so, עולא allows a פסח to be offered for him. Why should the slaughtering time matter for the traveler but not for the טמא שרץ?

keyTerms.meaning: A person made impure by touching a dead creeping creature. He becomes pure after immersing, at nightfall.
'We slaughter and sprinkle (the blood)' — the פסח is offered on his behalf
'But look!' — introduces a contradicting case

phrases.english: For you it is difficult, since you said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לִיכָּנֵס בִּשְׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה,
phrases.english: 'Anyone who cannot enter at the time of slaughtering.'
But a person impure from a שרץ
also cannot enter at the time of slaughtering,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָאָמְרַתְּ: שׁוֹחֲטִין וְזוֹרְקִין עַל טְמֵא שֶׁרֶץ.
phrases.english: and yet you say: we slaughter and sprinkle on behalf of one impure from a שרץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first half of רבה's challenge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal inconsistency. Being unable to enter at slaughtering time exempts the traveler, but it does not stop us from offering for a טמא שרץ.

steps.title: Challenge to רב יהודה from a טמא שרץ
steps.stepSummary: A טמא שרץ can enter by eating time, yet רב יהודה forbids slaughtering for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רב יהודה it is difficult, since he said: anyone who cannot enter at the time of eating. But a טמא שרץ can enter at the time of eating, and yet he said: we do not slaughter and sprinkle for a טמא שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה shows the opposite problem for רב יהודה. The טמא שרץ will be pure by eating time, yet רב יהודה does not let us bring the פסח for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יהודה, the only thing that matters is whether a person can arrive by eating time. A טמא שרץ can do that, since he becomes pure at night. So by רב יהודה's own logic, we should offer the פסח for him, yet רב יהודה says we do not. עולא answers both challenges starting in step 27; his defense of רב יהודה continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And yet he says' — points to a contradiction with his other ruling
'We do not slaughter' — the פסח is not offered for him

steps.whatToRemember: The טמא שרץ case cuts both ways. For עולא, he is like a traveler at slaughtering time but is still included. For רב יהודה, he can make it by eating time but is still excluded.

phrases.english: And for Rav Yehuda it is difficult, since he said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לִיכָּנֵס בִּשְׁעַת אֲכִילָה,
phrases.english: 'Anyone who cannot enter at the time of eating.'
But a person impure from a שרץ
can enter at the time of eating,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָאָמַר: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין וְזוֹרְקִין עַל טְמֵא שֶׁרֶץ!
phrases.english: and yet he says: we do not slaughter and sprinkle on behalf of one impure from a שרץ!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the second half of רבה's challenge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal inconsistency. If being able to arrive by eating time is what counts, the טמא שרץ qualifies, yet רב יהודה excludes him.

steps.title: עולא says neither view is difficult
steps.stepSummary: עולא replies to רבה that the טמא שרץ case is not a problem for his view or for רב יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (עולא) said to him: It is not difficult for me, and it is not difficult for רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא pushes back on both of רבה's challenges at once. This line sets up the next moves, where he will explain each view separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה claimed the טמא שרץ case breaks both definitions of דרך רחוקה. עולא says it breaks neither. He states this as a headline, and the explanations come right after, starting with his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: For me / according to my view
A difficulty, a problem

phrases.english: He (Ulla) said to him (Rabbah):
It is not difficult for me
phrases.notes: He's standing up for his own definition, the one based on the time of slaughtering.

phrases.english: and it is not difficult for Rav Yehuda.
phrases.notes: He's also standing up for רב יהודה's definition, the one based on the time of eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא לְדִידִי קַשְׁיָא וְלָא לְרַב יְהוּדָה קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבה's double challenge from steps 24 to 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General denial of the difficulty, with details to follow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה thought the טמא שרץ case contradicts both definitions of דרך רחוקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא holds that both definitions survive. The explanations follow.

steps.title: Far journey applies only to a pure person
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the rule of דרך רחוקה applies only to a טהור person, so the טמא שרץ case is not covered by it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For me it is not difficult: the rule of a far journey applies to someone who is pure, and there is no rule of a far journey for someone who is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא defends his own view. He says the 'far journey' measure applies only to a person who is טהור. A טמא person is judged by different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's challenge was this: a טמא שרץ also cannot enter the עזרה at slaughtering time, yet we still slaughter the פסח for him. עולא answers that his slaughtering-time test only measures distance for a person who is טהור. A טמא person's status follows the laws of טומאה, not the far-journey rule. So the טמא שרץ case is a separate category and does not contradict his definition.

keyTerms.meaning: A far journey, which exempts a person from bringing the פסח on time
Ritually pure
Ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not saying a טמא person may never bring the פסח. He is only saying that a טמא person's status is not measured by the far-journey test. It is decided by the laws of טומאה instead.

phrases.english: For me it is not difficult:
the rule of a far journey is for the pure person,
phrases.notes: The slaughtering-time test measures distance only for someone who is pure.

phrases.english: and there is no rule of a far journey for the impure person.
phrases.notes: An impure person is handled by the laws of טומאה, so the טמא שרץ case is a separate matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידִי לָא קַשְׁיָא: דֶּרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה לַטָּהוֹר, וְאֵין דֶּרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה לַטָּמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the general answer from step 27 by defending עולא's own view against the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule (it applies only to a טהור person)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any person who cannot enter at slaughtering time, even a טמא שרץ, should count as being on a דרך רחוקה under עולא's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The far-journey measure applies only to someone who is טהור. A טמא person's case is decided by the laws of טומאה, so slaughtering for a טמא שרץ does not contradict עולא.
